prompt:
Use case: highly photorealistic real-world animal photographs for a children's Hanzi lesson; one vertical triptych source to be cropped into three landscape photos.
Canvas and layout: exactly 1024x1792 pixels. Three independent edge-to-edge horizontal landscape photographs stacked vertically in equal thirds. Top photo occupies y=0 through 596, middle y=597 through 1194, bottom y=1195 through 1791. Hard scene changes only at y=597 and y=1195. No gutters, separator lines, borders, inset frames, gradients between panels, text, labels or watermarks.
Top photograph: one real black-and-white spotted cow standing naturally in a simple green pasture, three-quarter side view. Show its entire body and all visible legs and hooves, both ears and its whole tail, with generous space around it.
Middle photograph: one real horned brown cow standing naturally in an uncluttered pasture, three-quarter view clearly showing both horns and ears. Full body, anatomically correct legs, hooves and tail completely inside the row with generous clearance.
Bottom photograph: one real cow eating a small pile of hay at ground level beside an open, daylight-lit farm shelter. A natural quadrupedal feeding posture with neck and head lowered; its entire body, ears, legs, hooves and tail are inside the photograph. Hay and shelter remain secondary.
Style and light: genuine documentary livestock photography, soft natural daylight, realistic short fur and individual hairs, natural eyes, textured wet nose, accurate bovine proportions and anatomy, subtle real-world imperfections, believable grass and hay. Each animal is clear and prominent but occupies no more than about 75 percent of its panel width and height; ample breathing room around extremities.
Constraints: exactly one cow in each row. No humans, anthropomorphism, clothing, cartoons, illustrations, CGI, 3D renders, toys, plastic surfaces, oversized eyes, extra or fused limbs, duplicated heads, cropped ears, horns, feet or tails. All three panels must look like real photographs.
